utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Sayers:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Ribicic. When we broke yesterday, we were just going over some of the significant developmental steps taken by the HVO on July the 3rd of 1992, and there are three documents that I would like you to take a look at in the HVO binder. The first one is at tab 7, sir. It's the decree on the armed forces of the HZ HB. Now, Dr. Ribicic, this is one of the first decrees that actually addresses the organisation of the armed forces of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a few items on this document, sir. If you would turn to Article 17, it's true, is it not, that the initial organisational structure of the armed forces of the HVO, the military component of the HVO, if you like, envisaged that the head of the defence department would designate commands and staffs of the armed forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that the Department of Defence would oversee the combat readiness of commands, staffs, and institutions; is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The next article of significance, and the last one relating to this document, is Article 29, sir. I believe that the translations that we received from the Prosecution in the front of this document, the English translations, are slightly inaccurate. I'd just like you to confirm, sir, that the supreme commander of the armed forces of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna is actually the president of the Community, that is, Mr. Mate Boban, and not the president of the presidency; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The next document, sir -- we've already addressed this yesterday, so I won't spend any time on it -- is tab 9 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sayers, to be able to understand, I should like to ask the witness, what is the difference between the president of the Community and the president of the presidency? You said that the president -- that the supreme commander of the armed forces of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna is the president of the Community, who is Mate Boban, and not the president of the presidency. What is the precise difference between the two, please? And who was the president of the presidency?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I can clear that point up with a question or two to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me put it to you, Dr. Ribicic, that as of July the 3rd, 1992, the same day that the decree on the armed forces was passed, we see a new amended decision that basically sets out the legislative, executive, and administrative structure of the HZ HB, and that was tab 2 of the first volume of exhibits dealing with the HZ HB; would you agree with that, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, sir, that the presidency of the HZ HB was actually the legislature of the Community; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, as of the 3rd of July onwards. Up until the 3rd of July, 1992, Mr. Boban performed only one function, and that was the function of president of the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. It was only as of the 3rd of July that the new function was put into place, that is to say, the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. After that document, dating from the 3rd of July onwards, Mr. Boban performed two functions simultaneously; he was at the same time president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and president of the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Some of the competencies he performed by virtue of his first function and some by virtue of his second function, and this division of competencies was not always exactly and precisely defined. But the fact remains that the function of supreme commander of the armed forces of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, he did perform as president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that elucidation, and it is a subtle one, Dr. Ribicic. But what you're saying, I believe, is that up until July the 3rd, 1992, there was simply a presidency consisting of all of the members of the municipal bodies, and they elected a president of the presidency, vice-presidents of the presidency, and a secretary; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, with the addition that you keep emphasising the overall body, together with the 30 representatives -- made up of the 30 representatives of the municipalities, whereas I focus on the separate function. Especially at the time when the presidency was not sitting, he had -- the president and the two vice-presidents and the secretary of the presidency had these functions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. But just so we're clear, as of July the 3rd of 1992, you essentially had two bodies: You had a president who, amongst his other functions, was the supreme commander of the armed forces, pursuant to the decree of the armed forces, as we've seen; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you had a presidency which, under Article 7 of the amended decision, also passed on July the 3rd, 1992, was the legislative body of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, that is, the body that actually passed the laws; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That was according to the provisions. But yesterday I warned you that in certain cases, it came about that the vice-president of the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna would sign certain enactments as the deputy-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna; that is, performing the function which on paper in the normative acts did not exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me just turn to two other documents, sir. If you'd just turn to tab 8 on volume 2, a document that has already been introduced into evidence as Exhibit D140/1. This was a decision on ranks in the HVO --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you slow down, please, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab 8, Dr. Ribicic, on the big volume there.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've seen this document before, I take it, sir.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a rank structure imposed on the military arm of the HVO as of July the 3rd of 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the last document in this series that I'd like you to look at is tab 10, sir, a decision on salaries and other remunerations for members of the armed forces, passed on the same day, July 3rd, 1992. The only article to which I'd like to draw your attention is Article 5, dealing with the military police. It says, sir, that: "Members of the military police, being an integral part of the armed forces, shall have the same rights as other members of the armed forces." And that is consistent with your understanding of the functioning of the military police within the armed forces generally; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct as far as salaries and other remuneration, but this particular decree and decision refers to salaries alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me just ask you to turn to tab 12, which is an order signed by the commander of the Central Bosnia HVO staff, Tihomir Blaskic, dealing with certain organisational matters, and it's entered the day after the July the 3rd, 1992 series of decrees dealing with the armed forces. Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have never seen this order before, but I looked at it yesterday because I had your documents at my disposal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you agree, sir, that as of July of 1992, to the best of your knowledge, we see the first stirrings, if you like, of military organisation, a recognisable hierarchical chain of command evolving within the military arm of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. Up until that moment, the situation was such that it was not organised as a separate structure, and only with that date did this come about. My only limitation is something that I mentioned several times before, is that even before that date some documents were enacted and documents signed that were not in keeping with these new provisions governing structure, which are quite clear cut.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, it's true, is it not, sir, or do you know that the HVO was recognised as an integral and component part of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in two separate documents, one dated July the 21st, 1992, and entitled "An Agreement on Friendship and Cooperation Between the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Republic of Croatia," signed by Dr. Tudjman, the president of the Republic of Croatia, and Mr. Izetbegovic, the president of the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Are you familiar with that document?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's already been introduced into evidence, Dr. Ribicic, as Exhibit D98/1. In the interests of time, unless the Trial Chamber wishes, I won't put it on the ELMO, but I'll read to you a section. Paragraph 6 of the document says: "The armed component of the Croatia Defence Council, Hrvatsko Vijece Obrane, is an integral part of the united armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The Croatian Defence Council will have its representatives in the joint command of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Provisional civil authorities established in wartime conditions within the scope of the Croatian Defence Council will be made to conform as soon as possible, with the constitutional juridical system of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina," and there are other parts of that paragraph not material to my question. But the question is, sir, that you were aware, as of July 1992, that the president of Bosnia-Herzegovina had actually signed an international document that recognised the HVO as a component of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to emphasise, with regard to this document, that in many aspects it is not in conformity with the situation on the ground and the kind of policy that was being waged by the HDZ and a portion of the official policies of the Republic of Croatia that I spoke about yesterday. So the signatories are advocating a state of affairs which, according to my conviction, would be the best possible one. But as I say, this was not in keeping with the policy waged in the opposite direction, nor did it correspond to the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, sir. Are you aware that the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina actually enacted a decree on the 6th of August, 1992, just a few days after the agreement that I've just described, entitled "A Decree with the Force of Law on Amendments to the Decree with the Force of Law on the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina"? Have you seen that decree before?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's true that under Article 1 of that decree, sir, that HVO forces would be an integral part of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: For the trial court's information, the exhibit number on that -- it's already in evidence -- D4/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that brings us to the Constitutional Court decision that you described, sir, September the 18th, 1992, passed by the Constitutional Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Let me just ask you, sir, that the constitution that the Constitutional Court was interpreting was actually the constitution of the Socialist Federal Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, was it not?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Constitutional Court had the function of working according to the constitutional provisions, on the basis of which it was institutionalised itself. It was the constitution of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, with all the amendments that were enacted up until that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, is it not, that the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina itself had not, as of this time, adopted its own constitution, had it, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, at the time, did have a constitution which, in many respects, had already been amended, but at that particular time, no amendments had yet been made to the provision concerning the name of the republic itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so that everyone is on the same wavelength, we are talking about the constitution of 1972 [sic], adopted by the Socialist Federal Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that the translation was correct, and the date mentioned was 1974. Is that right: the Federal Republic? Is that what you're asking?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question? Maybe there was a translation difficulty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that the constitution to which you've alluded is the 1974 constitution adopted by the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, part of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's true that it was the 1974 constitution which was adopted by the assembly of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which at the time was one of the six republics making up the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. But that constitution was amended later on, and I should like to warn you that, for example, in Slovenia, the provision was amended as to the name of the republic itself, but that is not the key change that had been made. The key changes had been made earlier and referred to the economic and political system, the possibility of a multi-party competition and multi-party elections, and so on and so forth. So that the constitution which was in force in 1992 was fundamentally different from the constitution that was adopted in 1974, and this was not true in equal measure for the Slovenian and Bosnia-Herzegovinian constitution, but in the case of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that constitution was fundamentally amended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your new country of Slovenia, though, sir, you would agree that the country adopted its own constitution following the declaration of independence by your country in 1991; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is so, but the fact remains that the constitutional changes in Slovenia, not only before it became independent and autonomous but also before the first multi-party elections, wielded substantial amendments to the constitution, so that we can no longer call it the constitution of the Former Socialist Republic of Slovenia, because, as I say, it was amended in substance with a great deal of amendments. This was not done in equal measure in Bosnia-Herzegovina, but some vital changes of economic and political life were adopted in Bosnia-Herzegovina as well, before and after the first multi-party elections took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's just get down to the basics here, Dr. Ribicic. It's true, is it not, that after Slovenia declared independence, it adopted its own new constitution; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But we cannot compare the 1974 constitution, which was also enacted in --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, but that was a simple question. The follow-on question is that Bosnia-Herzegovina, after the declaration of its independence and at the time of the Constitutional Court decision in September of 1992, had not adopted its own brand new constitution, had it?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes. But the new constitution does not change the 1974 constitution but the situation which was prevalent at the time; that is to say, the 1974 constitution was significantly amended by the amendments, changed by the amendments, and that is where the difference is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the amendments you're talking about are the 1988 amendments; isn't that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1988, those amendments were enacted at a federal level, amendments to the federal constitution, which is no longer relevant here. In 1989 and subsequently, other new amendments were adopted, amendments to the republican constitutions, which wielded a vital change in the constitutional system of Bosnia-Herzegovina as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether any amendments were adopted after March the 6th of 1992, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let me proceed to the next related subject on this and just a few short questions. In connection with the Constitutional Court decision, it's true, is it not, that no notice was given to the HZ HB authorities, as far as you know? That's correct, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it is correct. I believe notice was given in the Official Gazette, that it was published in the Official Gazette of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and thereby notice of this was given to all interested parties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me be more precise, Dr. Ribicic. Before the decision was actually reached, you would agree with me that no notice was given to the authorities of the HZ HB that the proceedings had actually been instituted; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen several documents where the Constitutional Court addresses other bodies of the republic -- and other bodies of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, referred to the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, with the request that all documents enacted should be submitted to them, because the government had made the decision that proceedings be initiated before the Constitutional Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question was very simple, Dr. Ribicic. You're not aware that any advanced notice was given or any notice of any type was given by the Constitutional Court to the authorities of the HZ HB that proceedings to declare the HZ HB unconstitutional under the constitution of the former socialist republic, no notice of those proceedings was given to the HZ HB; isn't that correct? As far as you know.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about the documents of the Justice Ministry, and I think this was an internal document. I know the public conclusions made by the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which adopted a clear stand that it was a case of formation contrary to the constitution, and clearly stated that because of that it would be initiating proceedings before the Constitutional Court. I have no information about any other direct contacts between the Constitutional Court and the organs of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're not in a position to tell the Trial Chamber that the authorities of the HZ HB were either informed that such a judicial proceeding had been instituted or that they were given an opportunity to participate in the presentation of evidence or the deliberations of the Constitutional Court; is that so, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Constitutional Court instituted proceedings upon its own initiative and the public was informed about it. As for direct contacts, I'm only aware of those contacts according to which the Constitutional Court was requesting documents and acts passed by the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. I have a short document signed by the president of the Constitutional Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Dr. Ismet Dautbasic, who -- and this document was sent to the Croatian Community of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and they tried to get documents from the HDZ party, and in this letter, reference is made that proceedings had been instituted regarding the constitutionality issue. I'm not quite sure, therefore, how the Constitutional Court gained possession of those documents, but I assume they must have received them from the authorities of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you actually have no information that that was so; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, except for what I have just said. I have no other documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the date of that short document to which you have just referred, sir, if you can tell?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have two documents in front of me. One is the 6th of August, 1992 and the other is the 31st of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where they were sent specifically?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were sent to the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that have been in Sarajevo, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, it was in Sarajevo. As far as I know, the Constitutional Court tried in various ways to get hold of those documents because they were aware that they existed and that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was functioning and functional, that those acts had still not been published in the Official Gazette which did not come out before September 1992. That is why the Constitutional Court wanted to gain possession of the original documents on the basis of which it could rule and make progress with the proceedings that it had instituted at its own initiative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree with me that Sarajevo at this time was surrounded by forces of the Bosnian Serb army and cut off from the rest of the country; correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether this request that was sent apparently to the offices of the HDZ in Sarajevo ever made its way to Mostar or to the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna authorities, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know very well that what I have in front of me cannot be sufficient for me to claim that the authorities of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna received this request and participated in the proceedings. I have mentioned it only as evidence that the Constitutional Court did try to obtain those documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Two final documents to which I'd like your attention drawn. Were you aware that General Sefer Halilovic and Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic signed an agreement on the 20th of April, 1993, which was seven months, I believe, after the Constitutional Court decision to which you've adverted, and paragraph 1 said: "The BiH army and HVO are both legal military forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and are treated equally."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just for the Trial Chamber's information, that document has been marked as D24/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not seen that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. One final document to which I'd like to draw your attention, this has already been admitted into evidence as Exhibit D27/1, is an agreement that was reached between Mr. Alija Izetbegovic and Mr. Mate Boban on April the 24th, 1993, announced in Zagreb, and the final attachment to that document is entitled, "Command Structure for the BiH Army and the HVO," and that the first paragraph of that document stated that "The BiH army and the HVO will retain their separate identities and command structures. Their functions will include all aspects of personnel, logistics, administration, training, morale, and identity." Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, I just know that there were repeated efforts to regulate things in the way envisaged by this document, and in fact I think that would have been the best solution, in my opinion, from the beginning, because then a war would not have broken out. But I've not had occasion to study that document specifically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But would you agree, sir, that the president of the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is, President Izetbegovic, actually signed a document seven months after the Constitutional Court decision which actually recognised the HVO as a legal, integral component of the armed forces of the republic?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Ribicic. Let's just proceed on chronologically. If you'd turn to tab 13 of the HVO volume upon which you have your hands. Tab 13. Were you aware that the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna had held a meeting at Grude on August the 14th of 1992 and that part of the items under consideration were the consideration of changes on the decree of the armed forces, changes to the regulations on military discipline, and the adoption of criminal law decrees?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you aware that Dr. Jadranko Prlic was appointed president of the HVO of the HZ HB on that day? And if you just turn to tab 14, that might help you.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have that. That's right, on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you turn to the next tab, tab 15, Mr. Stipo Ivankovic of Odzak was appointed vice-president of the HVO of the HZ HB; is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you just take a look at the next tab, it's true, is it not, that the HVO adopted -- and I address your attention specifically to the phraseology of this decree, sir -- the HVO adopted a decree on the application of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Criminal Code of the SFRY -- and this is important, I think -- "in time of the immediate threat of war or time of war on the territory of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna." You are aware that that decree had been adopted; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have studied that document. It is particularly interesting because it is not only a matter of the application of the republican code but also the federal criminal code which was taken over by the republic. But I should like to point out that that legislation was valid in the area we are referring to. This decree, on the one hand, showed or reflected the efforts of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna to decide, in a sovereign and independent manner, which legislation will be implemented and which will not on its territory. The second point I should like to make is when things are solved in this way -- and a similar step was taken in Slovenia, that is, the takeover of federal or republican laws -- that its contents are thereby substantially changed, in the sense that that criminal legislation acquires a new role. It is no longer in the service of the defence of those states for which it was adopted but in the defence of institutions and citizens of states which are taking over those regulations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Ribicic. But there was only one point that I wanted to address to your attention. It's true, is it not, that as a temporary, expedient measure, under wartime conditions, the HVO decided to adopt the Criminal Code of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, not any other state, as its criminal law; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The period to which this decree applies, I have always emphasised that they were laws that were valid during the immediate threat of war or time of war, even in the case of regulations that did not have any direct links to the military situation, such as, for instance, regulations concerning the Automoto Association, or things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One final question on this decree, Dr. Ribicic. You would agree, would you not, that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, had it wished, certainly could have adopted, I suppose, the Criminal Code of the Republic of Croatia, but it didn't, did it?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, sir. Now, the next document to which I would like to draw your attention is a separate exhibit which I'd like to have handed out, and it's an excerpt from the minutes of the meeting of Croatian Defence Councils in municipalities of Central Bosnia on the 22nd of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D184/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do not believe that we have a Croatian original of this, Dr. Ribicic, so you will have to bear with me as I translate this. There are only a couple of provisions of this document that I want to draw to your attention. The first appears on the page that's stamped on the bottom right-hand side "00320380," and let me just read to you two entries. The first is in the middle of the page, and it says: "Military HVO authorities are asked to speed up the process of making the military formations more professional, of introducing order into military circles, and making the military police professional. They should also put an end to military war profiteers." The second is two entries below that, and it says: "Military HVO authorities are requested to respect the prescribed procedure for arresting individuals suspected of having committed illegal deeds in order to protect the legal security of citizens." Then the last part of this document to which I'd like to draw your attention is on the last page, sir, just three items up from the bottom, and it says: "The Ministry of Defence of the HZ HB and the military command are requested to issue regulations on military jurisdiction in order to avoid a conflict of jurisdiction between the military and the civilian government." Let me just ask you, sir: It's right, isn't it, that around this time, between July and October, and this document is representative of this, you can see the military organs of the armed forces of the HVO coalescing, organising, becoming clearer, and separating from the civilian organs of government; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Along those lines, I wonder if I could now address the second seminal date which we would submit exists in the legislative evolution and military evolution of the HVO, which is October the 17th, 1992. Two matters of detail. Could you turn to tab 18, sir. You were aware, I take it, that Kresimir Zubak was appointed as the second vice-president of the HVO on that date, October the 17th, 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the next document chronicles the appointment of the third vice-president of the HVO, Mr. Anto Valenta; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Now, the next document is a document that you've described in your report as a very comprehensive document, the decree of the armed forces of the HZ HB, tab 20, and it's also dated October the 17th, 1992. I just wanted to touch very lightly on some salient features of this substantial decree, and it needn't delay us too long. Would you agree, sir, that under Article 9 and Article 10 of this extensive decree, it was the defence department of the HZ HB that essentially controls the armed forces, that was responsible for drawing up defence plans, drawing up agreed policy, and plans for use of the armed forces, as well as setting up systems of leading and commanding the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have reviewed this document last night again, and that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, indeed, Dr. Ribicic. If you would just turn to Article 11, I'd like you to agree with me and assure the Trial Chamber that the general staff would be founded by the defence department and that the structure of the general staff would be prescribed by this supreme commander, which we now know is the president of the HZ HB "who shall appoint the general staff leadership." You'd agree with that, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is envisaged by the provisions of Article 11, and the organisation of the general staff is prescribed by the supreme commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. Could you just turn to Article 25, and I'd just like you to agree that political activity in the armed forces, including the formation of parties and organisation of political meetings and manifestations, was prohibited.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says, but it is another matter what influence this had in practice, because the composition of the presidency consisted of the leaders of all branches of government and all military authorities, and they all belonged to one and the same party, the HDZ, so that this prohibition can be a restriction. It is a normal provision contained in all modern constitutional laws, but in this context it was a limitation on the activity of other parties. All the documents of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna specifically mentioned the important role and significance of the Croatian Democratic Union, the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate your views, Dr. Ribicic, but you would agree that it was only in the context of the army, the armed forces of the HZ HB, that political activity was prohibited; right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But it is also correct that the supreme commander was at the same time the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and a member of the HDZ, which was a component part of the HDZ of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. As you've just said, and if you just turn to Article 29, you'll see that the supreme commander of the HZ HB armed forces shall be the president of the HZ HB, and that among his duties was the duty to issue regulations on military discipline and other instructions; you would agree with that, right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And the final question in connection with this document is Article 34, sir, which provides that: "Commanders of the armed forces shall be appointed and relieved of duty by the HZ HB president, but that commanders of brigades and high-ranking officers shall be appointed or replaced by the head of the defence department or by commanders appointed by him." The head of the Defence department at the time was Bruno Stojic; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain of the specific appointment you mention, but your interpretation of Article 34 is correct regarding the function of the president and the Defence department.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And one final general question in connection with this document. You would agree, would you not, that the vice-president of the presidency, either of them, had no power to appoint, to remove, or to discipline Operative Zone commanders, brigade commanders, or HVO soldiers under the decree on the armed forces? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're asking me from the point of the regulations and the formal legal prescriptions, that is right, but if you ask me from the standpoint of actual and factual relations on the ground and in reality, then the answer would not be that. I have seen that on a number of occasions, generally speaking, and also in specific cases to which this decree applies, that the practice deviated significantly from the regulations. The real influence of the vice-president of the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was something that can, with difficulty, be corroborated by documents, but it is a fact that his influence in practice was much greater than one would think, on the basis of these regulations that we have seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not aware -- let's talk about specifics here. You're not aware of any instance in which either of the vice-presidents of the presidency ever appointed an Operative Zone commander, a brigade commander, or a soldier to any position, are you? Any specific instance.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I know of cases when he signed certain documents as the vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Therefore, I am aware of certain documents which he signed in that function.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And several of those documents have been put before the Trial Chamber. But let me ask you a second question. You're not aware of any instance in which the vice-president or either of the vice-presidents of the presidency ever removed an Operative Zone commander or a brigade commander from their duties, are you?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any cases of appointments or removal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the same is true for instances of disciplinary proceedings being instituted involving the input of either of the presidents of the HZ HB presidency? You're not aware of any such instance, are you?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have mentioned these disciplinary proceedings a number of times now and the question of discipline. In that connection, I wanted to say that all those measures, which are certainly positive, especially those that you read from the decree, the aim being the formation of an armed force which would be disciplined and which would act in a military fashion, but, unfortunately, that is no guarantee that no deviations would occur. And when I reviewed the overall regulations on violations of criminal and other laws, I saw that those provisions define, with greater clarity, acts which relate to military matters, whereas other others --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but the question was simple, and we'll get on to the district military prosecutor's office in just a minute. But the question was: You're not aware of any specific instance in which either of the vice-presidents of the presidency of the HZ HB ever participated in any disciplinary proceedings instituted against an Operative Zone commander, a brigade commander, or a soldier, are you?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You interrupted me in the middle of a sentence. I just wanted to finish my thought, that the same did not apply to violations of humanitarian and international law. As for your question, I am not aware of any such instances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, if you turn to the next tab, sir, tab 21, it's a decree on the district military prosecutor's offices in the territory of the HZ HB in times of war or the immediate threat of war, and this decree was also passed on the 17th of October, 1992. I would just like to draw your attention to Article 4. Unlike appointments to the military armed forces, it's true, is it not, sir, that the district military prosecutor and his deputies were, in fact, to be appointed by the presidency of the HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to Article 4, the district military prosecutor supervises the work of district military prosecutor's officer, and he's accountable to the presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So as of October 17th, 1992 and thereafter, you would agree with me that the district military prosecutor's office was responsible for prosecuting the perpetrators of criminal acts falling within the jurisdiction of the military courts; correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would also agree that the district military prosecutor's office was responsible for undertaking necessary measures to uncover criminal acts and to request investigations; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, it was the duty of the district military prosecutor's office to collect --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you slow down, Mr. Sayers, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was the duty of the district military prosecutor's office to collect criminal complaints, and that's specifically recited in Article 6. Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The next document in the bundle that we've provided to the Trial Chamber and to you is a document that has already been marked Exhibit Z341.3, and it is tab 22 of this bundle. Just one very simple document -- question on this document, sir. This is the document dated November the 3rd, 1992 that sets up the home guard. Under Article 5, the home guard is subordinated to the command of the Operative Zones and to the general staff in the chain of command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you agree, sir, that by October the 17th, 1992, we can see a situation in which the civilian arm of the HVO and the military arm has largely been organised and that they exist with separate functions and separate competencies?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one final question along these lines, and I'll touch on this very lightly. If you would just turn to tab 25, sir. I don't know whether you've seen this decree -- this order before, but it's an order signed by Colonel Blaskic, the commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, setting up the command structure and the reporting structure, if you like, for the formation of that zone. Have you ever seen that document before?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw it yesterday for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. And then, if you turn to tab 27 and tab 26, you can see more orders issued by Colonel Blaskic dealing with matters relating to brigades and their municipalities, requests for names of brigades, and then finally, in March of 1993, there's a clarification on who precisely has the power to dismiss brigade commanders and other high-ranking officers. You saw those, I take it from your testimony, Dr. Ribicic, for the first time yesterday?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday already I said that I was not a military expert and that one of my conditions to prepare my analysis was to confine myself to matters of constitutional law. Therefore, the organisation, the structure of the army, interested me only from the point of view of the constitutional system, the organisation and structuring of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. I therefore cannot speak about personnel solutions or any other military affairs in any detail. But what you have now set out to prove, that is, that the supreme commander, who at the same time was the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, was the one who played a decisive and crucial role, I can confirm that. But I must add an aside, and I shall add it always, when this comes to constitutional law rather than military matters. In Bosnia-Herzegovina, many things that happened in practice were quite at odds with the things that were prepared, written down, and which the latter, I mean, were often done very professionally, but it was often varies with the practice in real life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Ribicic, just one final question in connection with the HVO bundle of documents, and I'd like you to turn to tab 24. Were you familiar with the decision dated November 18th, 1992, signed by the president of the HVO, Dr. Jadranko Prlic, establishing a personnel commission in the HVO and appointing five people to sit on it?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that and I went through that decision yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree, sir, that that is a relatively insignificant commission in terms of the overall institutions of government of the HVO and the overall military institutions that we've just reviewed in some detail?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I could really agree with you. The sphere of personnel is invariably one of the most important areas. It may look like it is not only the formal but also the informal influence on the appointment and the discharge of duties by very many people, so that I couldn't really say that it was an insignificant decision, but perhaps not as significant as those mentioned in some other documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. In connection with the testimony that you gave regarding citizenship issues -- actually, I didn't think you gave testimony on that, but there was certainly quite a bit of attention to that subject devoted in your report. Just two decrees I'd like to bring to your attention and get your views on these. The first one is dated February the 26th, 1993, signed by Dr. Prlic, and it's entitled "A Degree on Border Crossing and Traffic in the Border Area of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna in Times of War or the Immediate Threat of War." This has already been marked as Exhibit D20/1, and I'd just like to read to you Article 2, sir. It says: "The border area shall consist of a 100-metre-wide belt encompassing parts of the territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina within the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, including the mainland, rivers, lakes, and sea along the borderline." Would you agree, sir, that this decree, in February of 1993, recognises that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna exists on the territory or within the territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna emerged within the territory of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina as a former constituent republic of Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and, territorial speaking, it could not be exempted from the territory of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. But when you relate it to my report, I need to say that I interpreted all those documents in that same way when I read them for the first time. But it is really brought into question by those political attitudes which said that in public, and politically, we shall always speak that we are for an independent and sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina, but in practice we shall be working towards the integration of Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna with the Republic of Croatia. So that even though this may be the normative on the paper, and it says very clearly it is within the boundaries of Bosnia and it mentions the deep borders of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but what does it mean in real life? If it is part of the Croatian policy and the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, both worked towards the integration, so then it becomes merely a formality on the paper geared to concealing the real state of affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In line with the testimony that you just gave, sir, I would like to draw your attention to another document which I'd like to have marked as an exhibit, which is called "The Decree on the Application of the Law on Movement and Residence of Foreigners on the Territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna in the Event of War or an Immediate Threat of War."

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document will be marked D185/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we have it on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I have one for the ELMO, as the interpreters have requested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document contains a number of provisions, sir. Feel free to read them all if you wish, but the only one which I would like to draw to your attention is Article 2. If we could zoom in on that, please, so that the interpreters can see it. Isn't true, sir, that Article 2 of this decree, addressing essentially movement and residence of aliens, says that every person who is not a citizen of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina is, according to this decree, a foreigner or an alien?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And from the point of view of legal standard, that is not in dispute. But what happened to those citizens of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina who were not of Croat ethnicity, what happened to them in practice, that is a completely different matter. And how the -- very many things would not have happened if the members of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna complied with this article. And by "this," I mean transfers of people and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I'm through with that document and it can be removed from the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I told you that we were through with the HVO binder, but I regret to say that there's just one more tab to which I need to draw your attention, tab 23, and it deals with the establishment of a division of the Supreme Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna in times of war or the immediate threat of war. You have seen this document and it's referred to in your report, sir, so there's no need to go through it.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the fact of the matter is that the HZ HB did not establish its own Supreme Court. What it tried to do was to establish a department of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Mostar; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, except that this division was autonomous. It was no longer a division as interpreted by the regulations of Bosnia-Herzegovina; it was an independent Supreme Court which was simply called the division of the Supreme Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is how it emerged, but its organisation, the staffing policy, and so on and so forth, were determined and laid down by the bodies of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and had nothing to do with the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time. Even this word "division" is no longer mentioned subsequently, when the Croatian Community became the Croatian Republic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let's just take a look at that contention that you made in light of Article 4 of the decree here. It's true, is it not, that any citizen of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina who's a lawyer and who passed the judicial exam and who had five years of experience working in the court or on legal matters in other state bodies, as well as a lawyer who was a prominent legal expert, could be appointed as a judge in the division, and that he could be a Croat, Muslim, or Serb, or any other ethnicity; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Formally speaking, that is true, but in practice, this provision does not mean that -- does not come to that. It is quite clear that all the leading officers in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna were reserved for Croats and, moreover, Croats who were members of the HDZ. This holds true of the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. This also holds true of the HVO and all other key positions. So if this provision --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Ribicic, and that's this: Isn't it true that many judges in the high court in Travnik, Bosanski Brod, Mostar, Odzak, Derventa, and Orasje were actually Muslims and that they were appointed by the HZ HB to serve in that capacity?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This decree and -- I referred to the Supreme Court. That is a division of the Supreme Court. I was speaking about this in the Croat Community in Herceg-Bosna. I do not exclude the possibility that there were also some Muslim individuals, especially at lower tiers, but it is quite clear that those were Muslims who had embraced the programme of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna; that is, that they are defending the Croat interests, the interests of the whole Croat people, defending the historic Croat lands, and so on and so forth. I do hope you will agree with me that objectives defined in this manner cannot encourage members of other ethnic groups to discharge any key positions, any key functions in a community which is organised along those lines. That is what I meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Now, you've given quite a bit of testimony concerning your views as to the ostensible objectives of the HDZ BiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I'd like to have one more exhibit marked, which is the minutes of the meeting of the Second General Assembly of the HDZ BiH, held on November the 14th, 1992 in Mostar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D186/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before, Dr. Ribicic?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just address your attention to paragraph 18, which appears, at least in the English version, using the Registry's numbering system, page 5576 and 5575, up at the top right-hand corner. The OTP's numbering, I'm sorry. Would you agree, sir, or does it affect your opinion relating to the ostensible objectives that you've concluded the HDZ had to read an address from the president of the party, Mr. Boban, saying: "Last year we established the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna in BH, and with the very fact of its establishment, we said that we were the only Croats in BH," Bosnia-Herzegovina, "that BH was our state, the state of the Croats that lived there, but also the state of other peoples." Were you aware that Mr. Boban had made comments along these lines, sir, to the Second General Assembly of the HDZ, other than from looking at this document, which apparently you've not seen before?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about many statements in a similar vein, but the public policy -- the policy of the Croat -- the public policy of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was aimed at a sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina, even at a time when this organisation was -- the HDZ's policy was led by Mr. Kljuic. However, yesterday I quoted Mr. Boban, who, at a meeting in Zagreb one year before, said that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was formed so that at a later date, and when so decided by the leadership of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna or the HDZ, it could join the Republic of Croatia. So I agree that what Mr. Boban says here is in line with what I think is useful for Bosnia-Herzegovina and was in line with the constitutional organisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time. But I need to add, in order to understand this, to understand why Serb autonomous provinces were set up and the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was formed, they were all formed as monoethnic communities, and these communities, however, should continue as multiethnic. So this is my objection. Of course, what it says here, it is quite praiseworthy, but I'm not sure that it was quite straightforward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true also, sir, that Mr. Boban goes on to observe, and this is in the middle of page 5575 of this exhibit, that "At this moment, this territory is the home of not only the Croatian people but also of 250,000 Muslims, who owe their current freedom to the Croatian people who paid for it with their blood and their young lives." So Mr. Boban is recognising that it's not only Croats who live in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna but also a very significant number of Muslims too; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, I already said that it meant the incorporation of municipalities in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna in which -- in some of which Croats did not have even a relative majority, let alone an absolute majority, and I never claimed that only Croats populated those municipalities. If the views which you have just read out, if those views had underpinned the formation of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, then there would have been no misunderstandings with the Muslims or the war; they would have fought side by side against the attempts to -- against attempts to partition Bosnia-Herzegovina by Serb autonomous provinces. So these views are quite positive, but they run counter to what is said in the documents of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, notably those documents which are the basis of that particular Community. The decision on the foundation of that Community says something else and especially does not mention Muslims; and other peoples, you yourself have pointed out, are mentioned for the first time at the time when the HVO was founded, when it is said clearly that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna will also engage in the defence of other peoples, regardless of who may attack them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, sir. Have you ever spoken to Mr. Boban yourself?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever discussed with anybody in the leadership of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna what their real objectives were? Dr. Prlic, for example, Mr. Akmadzic, Mr. Buntic, people like that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was preparing my report, my opinion, I talked to many people who I thought were familiar, were conversant with the situation, and I asked 18 questions of them. But needless to say, I confined myself to questions of a constitutional law nature, and I had several meetings. I was not looking for politicians or political protagonists. I tried to establish contact with professors and other professions. The only one in this group who did hold a political position in Bosnia-Herzegovina was Mr. Kljuic. I did not meet him on that occasion; he answered my questions in writing. So I tried to work not only on the basis of regulations and enactments, but also on the basis of those discussions I had, of those interviews, in order to get a better picture of what was really happening in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. And in particular --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your answer is that you've not actually spoken to any of the leaders of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, but rather only to their political opponents; right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not. I sought interviews with those who, in my view, were best qualified to speak about it, who were familiar with the situation, and I also said that I would not be quoting them in this Tribunal without their permission, without their authorisation. But if the Court so desires, then we should have to go into a closed session and then I would name people that I spoke to. Most of them are Croats, if I may put it that way, and at least one of them, at least at a later stage, also held an important position in Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever speak to Dr. Prlic about what was going on in the HVO? He was, after all, sir, the president of the organisation, and who better than him to give you views on what the objectives of the organisation really were.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My opinion was the result of the study of normative enactments, testimonies, interviews, and what I read in various interviews and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a yes or no, Dr. Ribicic. Did you speak to Dr. Prlic?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. The question was somewhat broader. As for this question, no, I did not speak to Mr. Prlic. But I beg the indulgence of the Court to say this: I am ready to say who I spoke to in a closed session because I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There's no need. I'm sure we have your evidence and we don't need this kind of detail. Now, Mr. Sayers, do you have very much more? It's now 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: One more question on this document, and what I propose to do is to proceed to the HR HB after the break, if that's acceptable to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I trust that's not going to take too long.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I would hope, Mr. President, that I would be through by 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think you said an hour and a half yesterday, but very well; ask the last question about this document and then we'll break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you turn to paragraph 23, Dr. Ribicic, were you aware that there had been five vice-presidents of the HDZ BiH elected on November the 14th, 1992, and that Mr. Kordic was one of the five?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware that Mr. Kordic held that position, among others. I know I saw it in one document or another, but I can't remember exactly which one it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now until half past eleven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If we can speed up, we will be grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I would like to speed up as much as I can, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd appreciate your cooperation, Dr. Ribicic. The next items I would like to address are things about which you may or may not know a lot, the Vance-Owen Plan and the Owen-Stoltenberg Plan. You said you're not an expert in international law, sir.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I just know about it in general terms and as far as it is linked up with the decisions made by the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you taken the opportunity to review the ten constitutional principles that were a prominent feature of the Vance-Owen Plan?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen those principles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you would agree with me, sir, that one of the principles was reaffirmation of the importance of the concept of three constituent peoples; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, sir, the Vance-Owen Plan specifically envisaged that the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina adopted a constitution which shall recognise three constituent peoples. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, sir, that the Croat contingent led by Mr. Mate Boban was the first of the three primary constituent peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina to sign the Vance-Owen Plan; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true also, sir, that the ten provinces that were to be established under that plan were not to have any international legal personality but, rather, they were to be provinces which had democratically elected governments; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the Trial Chamber knows that the Vance-Owen Plan fell into significant disrepair in May of 1993, and after that, the next evolution of the constitutional solutions for the problems of Bosnia-Herzegovina proposed by the International Community was the Owen-Stoltenberg Plan. Are you familiar with the constitutional agreements that are part of the Owen-Stoltenberg Plan?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It would be fair to say, sir, that the Owen-Stoltenberg Plan, as reported to the Security Council on August the 6th of 1993 -- and this is already in evidence, Mr. President, Exhibit D141/1 -- it would be fair to say that the principal feature of this plan was three ethnic republics held together in a loose union? Would that be correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The name of each of the constituent republics was going to be determined by the competent authorities of that republic; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And indeed, the first article in the constitutional agreement provided: "The union of republics of Bosnia and Herzegovina is composed of three constituent republics and encompasses three constituent peoples, the Muslims, Serbs, and Croats, as well as a group of other peoples." You're familiar with that principle; right, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, are you also familiar with Annex C to the agreement -- which I would ask the usher to put on the ELMO -- which provided the human rights instruments incorporated into the constitutional agreement? I don't know if you've ever seen this document before, but if you'd just look at the item that we've put as Annex C to the exhibit. Have you ever read the human rights instruments incorporated into the constitutional agreement before?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you'd just leave that on the ELMO, or could you turn to the preceding page, because I'll have one question shortly about that. One final question in connection with the Owen-Stoltenberg Plan, sir, was this: It's true, is it not, that you are aware that none of the three constituent republics could withdraw from the union of Bosnia-Herzegovina without the prior agreement of all of the republics? You were familiar with that agreement, were you not?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you would put before you the -- I see you already have it. I'm going to skip by the announcement of the founding of this republic, sir, which is at tab 1, August the 28th, 1993, and I'd like to address your attention to the founding decision, which is found at tab 2. This founding decision, sir, is signed by a gentleman by the name of Perica Jukic, the president of the House of Representatives; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have spoken to Mr. Jukic, have you?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But in this way you will know who I talked to. If you go through the names one by one, the people I didn't talk to, you will be deducing this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just turn very quickly to a few articles that I'd like to draw to your attention and to that of the Trial Chamber. Article 5 first. The authority in the republic was to be derived from the people and shall belong to the people as a community of free and equal citizens; correct? Yes? You have to -- is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one question that I forgot to ask, sir. Would you agree that the HR HB was founded on August the 28th, 1993, about three weeks after the report of the Secretary-General to the Security Council regarding the Owen-Stoltenberg Plan; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke about the links between the two yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Article 6 provided that in this new republic of constituent peoples, the Republic was to be a parliamentary democracy, with legislative authority to be exercised by the House of Representatives; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this decision, the most important changes, in my opinion, are in the preamble itself, as the positive changes that I spoke about yesterday, and the changes as in Article 11. But as a counterbalance, you have the last two articles, that is to say, Articles 11 and 12, where the emphasis is on continuity of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna and as far as the legal set-up is concerned and the realisation of the basic functions of power and authority. So we have the provision there that the function of a state authority, according to the provisions of this decision, will be performed by the bodies of government of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, which means that the functioning of the Republic of Herceg-Bosna, we have the production of documents from the old system. And it would be difficult to say that that old system meant a division of power into legislative, administrative, and other operative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Dr. Ribicic, it specifically provides that legislative authority is to be exercised by the House of Representatives. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And executive authority is to be exercised by the government; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And judicial authority, of course, to be exercised by the courts; right?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If we compare other documents and this division of power and authority, what we can notice is that the House of Representatives does have a somewhat stronger function than in other European parliamentary systems, from the British system onwards, and this relates to the relationship between the House of Representatives and the government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. As you can see from Article 7, the president of the government was to be elected by the House of Representatives. That speaks for itself. But other article I'd like to draw to your attention is Article 8, which states specifically that the president is the supreme commander of the armed forces, and it is the president who appoints and dismisses high-ranking military holders of office; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as Article 7 is concerned, let me state that it is not usual in parliamentary systems, but that it is the head of state who usually appoints the government. As far as Article 8 is concerned, it stresses the function of the president of the republic for the united functioning of all governmental bodies; that is true, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's basically a continuation of the same principle that we saw enshrined in the armed forces decree, Article 29, which provided that had the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was the supreme commander of the armed forces of the HVO; correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Because usually in the countries of Europe, in formal terms, the president of the republic in parliamentary systems is the commander of the armed forces, but in practice, those functions are largely formed by the government, whereas in Herceg-Bosna, that function of the president of the republic has been designed in stronger terms. So I can say that the government was left on two sides by the representative organs and by the head of state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could I ask you to turn to the next tab, tab 3, which deals with a decision on constituting the House of Representatives of this new republic passed simultaneously with the basic decision. This is also signed by Perica Jukic, I believe, sir. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Article 1 of this decree specifically provides that it is the House of Representatives that is the supreme representative body vested with legislative power. Would you agree, sir, that the House of Representatives assumed the functions that were essentially performed by the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is only true up to a point. It assumed the functions which relate to legislation and legislative powers, and, in part, functions by which he established and determined the cadre's composition and steered the work of the government. The other functions which the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna performed, executive functions, the House of Representatives, those were not assumed by him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, would you just turn to Article 19 of this decision, sir? It specifically states that the powers of the presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna shall be assumed by the House of Representatives, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.
